en: Contrary to popular belief, Jose Rizal advocated for peaceful educational reforms rather than an armed revolution against Spain.
Although proclaimed in 1898, Philippine Independence Day was celebrated on July 4 until President Diosdado Macapagal changed it to June 12 in 1962.
Many assume the President declares war, but the Philippine Constitution grants Congress, not the President, the sole power to declare a state of war.
Despite common rumors, the Sampaguita, not the Waling-waling, remains the official national flower of the Philippines, officially declared in 1934.
Contrary to the belief that it is merely an American Sign Language dialect, Filipino Sign Language is a distinct, legally recognized national sign language.
Contrary to the misconception that it is a single tribe, Igorot is an umbrella term for several distinct Austronesian ethnolinguistic groups in the Cordilleras.
While often misunderstood as pure Tagalog, the national language Filipino is legally mandated to be enriched based on all existing native Philippine languages.
Despite common assumptions, the Philippine Bill of Rights guarantees fundamental civil liberties, including due process and equal protection, to all persons, including minors.
Many think Fe del Mundo was only a pediatrician, but she also invented a makeshift bamboo incubator using hot water bottles for rural areas.
Contrary to local assumptions, Juan Luna painted his masterpiece Spoliarium in Madrid, Spain, where it won a gold medal at the 1884 Madrid exposition.
Though rooted in pre-colonial dance, the Sinulog festival is actually a Christianized devotion honoring the Santo Niño, introduced by Spanish missionaries after 1521.
While famously depicted as moving a nipa hut, bayanihan actually encompasses a broader cultural value of communal unity and helping neighbors in any crisis.
